overview:
CAMT — Cyber Advanced Threat Modeling Tool

Purpose
CAMT combines cyber-security analysis, CTI, network discovery, Digital Twin, forensics, evidence handling, reporting and modular investigation workflows.

CAMT Workspace
Home is the primary landing page. It presents the main capabilities: Network Analysis, Intelligence & Research, Forensics & Evidence, Security Analysis, Reporting & Presentation, and Projects & Cases.

Modules and plugins
Installed capabilities are discovered dynamically. Modules and plugins can provide category, description and artwork metadata. Repository/Module Manager is the management layer for installed, available and updateable packages.

Recommended workflow
1. Start from Home and select a capability.
2. Open a core function or installed module.
3. Create or load investigation data.
4. Correlate findings across Network, Intelligence, Security and Forensics.
5. Use Projects & Cases for project-bound context.
6. Generate technical or management output through Reporting.

Important
Threat Actor and similarity scores are analytical indicators, not attribution. Record evidence, confidence, negative evidence and source quality.
quickstart:
Start
1. Open CAMT. Home displays the capability landing page.
2. Choose Network, Intelligence, Forensics, Security, Reporting or Projects.
3. Select a capability card to see available core functions and installed modules.
4. Use Home or Ctrl+Home to return to the landing page.

Repository
Use Repository/Module Manager to inspect installed, available and updateable packages. Future GitHub packages can provide their own category and artwork metadata without a CAMT core rebuild.

Projects
Project details and project-oriented controls are only relevant when Projects & Cases is active.
workspace:
CAMT Workspace
Home is the primary 1.2.0 Beta 9 landing page. It is capability-first, not a project dashboard.

Primary capability areas
- Network Analysis
- Intelligence & Research
- Forensics & Evidence
- Security Analysis
- Reporting & Presentation
- Projects & Cases

Navigation
The normal CAMT menu bar remains available in the main application. Capability pages should open inside the main window. Use Home or Ctrl+Home to return.

Dynamic content
Home combines core navigation contributions with installed module metadata. New modules should declare category, description and artwork rather than being hardcoded into CAMT core.

Projects
Project tree, project details and project-specific controls belong to the Projects view and are intentionally separated from Home.
scenario:
Scenario Intelligence processes TXT, Markdown, JSON, DOCX, PDF and pasted text.

Analysis objects
- Assets
- Relationships
- Events
- Timeline
- Trust Zones
- ATT&CK / ATT&CK ICS
- Attack Paths
- Crown Jewels
- Choke Points
- Single Points of Failure
- Risk
- Mitigations
- Threat Actor Evidence

Source classification
CAMT distinguishes between:
- explicit scenario information;
- derived information;
- assumptions.

Run scenario
After scenario content changes, Run scenario re-runs the analysis and refreshes the
active scenario result.
digital_twin:
Network Digital Twin models a live, imported or designed infrastructure environment.

Main modes
- New / Empty
- New Scan / Load Scan
- Scenario Import / Load Scenario
- Visualize
- Live
- Scenario
- Compare
- Timeline
- Attack Path

Design / What-if
Add nodes and intermediary devices, connect assets, remove elements, save a design, apply scenarios and run analysis. Design actions do not change the real network.

NetMap integration
Network Mapper discovers and builds a baseline. Network Digital Twin models and analyses. Network Visualisation presents topology and relationships.

Language
If literal keys such as dt.new_scan are shown, Digital Twin source and locale files are out of sync.
attack_path:
Attack Path uses the active analysis model.

Source
- Scan mode: scan model
- Scenario mode: scenario model
- Compare mode: combined model

The designer can generate attack paths from the active scenario. Nodes contain
asset, technique, risk and confidence information.

An attack path is an analytical route based on available relationships and events.
It is not automatically proof that the route was actually used.
cti:
Offline CTI
The local CTI library uses SQLite and can operate air-gapped.

Generic CTI ingestion
Use Intelligence Ingestion for pasted text, URLs, files or folders. Extraction is
first written to SQLite staging; only accepted candidates are committed. Threat
actors, campaigns, malware, tools, IOCs, relationships, aliases, sectors and ATT&CK
techniques are stored locally.

Threat Actor Assessment
The engine compares scenario evidence with actor profiles. Results are ranked with
score, confidence and supporting rationale.

Scoring Policies
Automatic: configured automatic weights are used.
Manual: user-defined weights are used.
Hybrid: automatic weight × user multiplier.

Behavioral Fingerprint
Intelligence > Behavioral Actor Fingerprint & Similarity compares an actor profile
or observed behavior pattern with the Actor Library. Intelligence Packs and Analysis
Profiles can extend the comparison without changing CAMT Core.

Review for each actor:
- supporting evidence;
- negative evidence;
- effective factor weighting;
- active policy;
- confidence;
- missing evidence.
intelligence_modules:
Modules are complete user-facing workflows or analysis capabilities. Plugins extend existing capabilities or providers.

Home integration
A module can declare category, description, icon or artwork. CAMT uses this metadata dynamically on Home and in package management.

Repository
Repository/Module Manager manages installed and available packages. Repository metadata can provide package URL, SHA-256, version, category and artwork.

Compatibility
Older packages without category/artwork remain installable. Missing artwork must never break navigation or package management.
workflow:
Workflow Center contains fixed analysis tracks for:
- Scenario Intelligence
- CTI Attribution
- Digital Twin Analysis
- Incident Response

Each step has status and progress. A workflow can be resumed after restart. The
workflow opens existing suite functions; it does not implement a second analysis
engine.
reports:
Report Studio supports technical and management reporting.

Scenario reports can include:
- Scenario Summary
- Baseline Network Diagram
- Scenario Overlay
- Digital Twin
- Attack Path
- Timeline
- Risk / Coverage
- MITRE ATT&CK
- Trust Zones
- Crown Jewels
- Choke Points
- Single Points of Failure
- Threat Actor Assessment
- Evidence and mitigations

Images from Scenario Intelligence are stored as report media and rendered by Report
Studio. Manually added images are registered as evidence.

Supported Behavioral Match
Reports > Generate > Supported Behavioral Match Report uses the most recently saved
canonical analysis result. Ranking, similarity, coverage, confidence, matched
evidence, contradictions and missing/unknown evidence are therefore not recalculated
by a separate reporting engine.
storage:
Storage architecture — CAMT 1.0.1

SQLite:
- Offline CTI database: offline_intelligence.sqlite3
- Threat actors
- Campaigns
- Malware
- Tools
- IOCs
- CTI relationships
- Actor aliases
- Actor techniques
- Sectors and regions
- Intelligence packages
- CTI observations

Core data still backed by JSON:
- Scenario Import: scenario-import/scenarios.json
- Scenario Simulator: scenarios/scenarios.json
- Network Assets: network-assets/assets.json
- Attack Paths: attack-paths/attack_paths.json
- Scenario Projections: scenario-bridge/projections.json
- Control Mapping: control-mapping/mappings.json
- CTI Scoring Policies: cti/scoring_policies.json
- Workflow state: workflow_state.json
- Docking layouts: workspace_layouts.json
- Threat observations: threat-intelligence/observations.json
- Digital Twin context: cyber-digital-twin/context.json

Files intentionally kept file-based:
- imported scenario documents;
- exports (JSON, CSV, HTML, PDF, RTF, PNG, SVG);
- logs and crash reports;
- evidence files and hashes;
- language resources;
- plugin manifests;
- project source files.

Conclusion
CAMT has not yet been fully migrated to one central SQLite persistence layer. CTI
is SQLite-backed. Relational core data such as scenarios, assets, relationships,
attack paths, projections, mappings, workflow history and scoring policies are
candidates for migration to a central CAMT database. UI preferences and export
files do not need to be stored in SQLite.
airgap:
CAMT can be used without internet access for local analysis.

Available offline:
- Scenario Intelligence
- local CTI SQLite database
- Threat Actor Assessment
- Digital Twin
- Attack Path
- Timeline
- Scoring Policies
- reporting

CTI updates can be imported through a controlled offline package or STIX import. An
import is recorded in the local CTI package history.

Case transfer
Use Export Airgap Case Package to transfer a standalone investigation including
provenance and hashes. Team Import validates the package before a new central Team
Case is created.

CVE transfer
A locally populated CVE dataset can later be synchronized to the central Team CVE
Repository through CVE Repository Sync. You can choose the full local dataset or
only CVEs used in local network findings.
team:
Team Workspace enables central collaboration without replacing standalone research mode.

Main components
- Active Team Case: select and activate a central case.
- NetMap / Asset Intelligence can be published to the active Team Case.
- Collaboration & Locks shows active users, object locks and delete requests.
- Optimistic concurrency prevents silent overwriting of newer revisions.
- Version / Diff / Merge Studio compares two revisions and saves a merge as a new revision.
- Delete Approval & Restore uses a request/approval workflow; an object is archived first and can be restored.
- Central Evidence File Store keeps large evidence files outside PostgreSQL/SQLite BLOBs and records SHA-256, uploader, timestamp and case relation.

Airgap to Team
A standalone investigation can be exported as .camtcase. Team Import verifies
provenance and hashes. The original standalone case remains unchanged. Evidence from
the package can be transferred to the Central Evidence File Store.
cve_sync:
CVE Repository Sync links the local standalone CVE dataset to a central Team CVE Repository.

Open Tools > Database Manager > CVE Dataset.

Available synchronization modes
- Sync full CVE DB → Team: synchronizes local vulnerabilities, product/version rules and package rules.
- Sync used CVEs → Team: synchronizes only CVEs present in local Network Vulnerability Findings.

Merge behavior
- CVE ID is the primary identity.
- Existing central records are not blindly replaced.
- Newer or equally dated local records may update central records.
- Duplicates are prevented.
- Source client, user, timestamp, mode and optional Active Team Case are recorded in the sync log.

Use
This supports air-gapped or standalone CAMT installations that first work locally
with a CVE dataset and later make that intelligence available to the Team environment
in a controlled way.
network_mapper:
Purpose
Network Mapper discovers hosts and network context and creates a NetMap baseline for other CAMT capabilities.

Hybrid operation
Windows and Linux retain platform-specific discovery paths.

Recommended workflow
1. Select the target network/CIDR.
2. Run discovery.
3. Review discovered hosts.
4. Run service/version scanning where required.
5. Correlate available vulnerability/CVE data.
6. Save or pass the baseline to Digital Twin, comparison or visualisation functions.

Presentation
English labels should include Print, Send and Style. Dutch uses Afdrukken, Verzenden and Stijl.
visual_reports:
Visual Intelligence in Network Asset Intelligence

The reporting pipeline generates visualizations from the same analysis snapshot as
tables and text. Asset or relationship counts must therefore not differ between a
diagram and its report.

Automatic visualizations
- Network Topology
- Risk Network Map
- Service Exposure Map
- CVE Candidate Map
- Entry Points / Gateways
- Service Exposure Overview
- Risk / Coverage Overview

Scenario reports can additionally include:
- Baseline Network Diagram
- Scenario Overlay
- Attack Path
- Timeline
- ATT&CK / ATT&CK ICS
- Trust Zones
- Crown Jewels
- Choke Points / SPOF
- mitigations and assumptions

Check
If a report shows a different host count from Network Asset Intelligence, verify
which scan/import is active and regenerate the report from the same analysis snapshot.
simulation_lab:
CAMT Simulation Lab Bridge

Purpose
An analyzed environment can be exported as a neutral lab manifest so an external
Deploy Tool can build an isolated simulation environment.

Flow
PCAP / text / NetMap / scenario
→ Scenario Analysis / Network Digital Twin
→ Simulation Lab Export
→ *.camt-lab.json
→ external Proxmox Deploy Tool

Separation of responsibilities
CAMT analyzes, models, classifies observed/inferred/assumed information and exports
assets, relationships, zones, services and lab hints.
The Deploy Tool selects the Proxmox node, assigns VMIDs, maps templates, configures
storage/bridges/VLANs and performs deployment.

Safety
CVE candidates are exported as context. CAMT does not automatically build a
vulnerable VM from a CVE match alone. Controlled vulnerability reproduction should
use an explicitly approved lab profile.

OT
PLC/RTU/IoT assets can be described as simulator profiles when physical hardware is
unavailable or undesirable.
team_server:
CAMT Team Server

Architecture
CAMT Client → Team Server/API → central database + Evidence File Store.

Backends
- SQLite: suitable for local Team Server test/demo.
- PostgreSQL: recommended for real multi-client collaboration.

Important
Clients should not log directly into PostgreSQL. Only the Team Server knows the database DSN.

Local test
Server URL: http://127.0.0.1:8765
Backend: sqlite
Database DSN in client: empty
API token: same value as team_server_config.json.

Multi-client
Run Team Server on a central machine and use its IP/DNS name in clients. Ensure the configured TCP port is reachable.

Production
Use TLS/reverse proxy and preferably personal authentication rather than one shared
bearer token before exposing Team Server outside a trusted management network.
team_cases: Active Team Case and Case Data
collaboration:
Collaborative Version Control

Purpose
Multiple researchers must be able to work concurrently without one save silently
overwriting another researcher's work.

Mechanisms
- Presence: shows who is working in a case/object.
- Soft lock: warns that an object is being edited.
- Hard lock metadata: for objects requiring exclusive editing.
- Optimistic concurrency: every save states the base revision.
- Revision conflict: a stale save receives HTTP 409 and is not written.
- Immutable version history: every valid save creates a new revision.
- Conflict log and audit trail.

Version / Diff / Merge Studio
Two revisions can be viewed side by side. A unified diff marks additions and
removals. A merged version is always stored as a new revision; existing history remains intact.
delete_restore:
Shared research objects are not deleted immediately.

Workflow
1. Researcher creates a delete request with a reason.
2. Object remains while the request is pending.
3. Another authorized user can approve or reject.
4. Self-approval is blocked.
5. On approval, the current object is moved to object_archive.
6. Version history and audit trail remain available.
7. An archived object can later be restored as a new revision.

This prevents reports, findings or other case objects from disappearing without an explicit decision.
module_packages:
New CAMT packages should be self-describing.

Recommended metadata
- package id
- name and version
- entrypoint/navigation contribution
- functional category
- description
- icon or artwork path
- minimum CAMT version
- capabilities and optional dependencies

Presentation
Artwork belongs in the package or repository metadata. Home and Module Manager load it dynamically. Do not hardcode package-specific names or artwork into CAMT core.

Localization
CAMT core presentation uses locale keys. Package-specific localized metadata can be supplied by the package/repository.
actor_discovery_wizard:
Purpose
The wizard guides research from source material to potential threat actors with a
similar modus operandi. It uses existing CAMT engines; individual workspaces remain directly accessible.

Sources
- PDF and other supported documents;
- URL and remote PDF;
- pasted text or passage;
- news article or analyst note.

Full Investigation
1. Source
2. Extract
3. Behavioral Fingerprint
4. Analysis Profile & Weighting
5. Known Relations / Control Group
6. Behavioral Discovery
7. Review, Disposition & Analyst Notes
8. Deep Analysis
9. Scenario / Environment
10. Report

Quick Discovery
Source → Extract → Fingerprint → Discovery → Review → Report.

Guided and Expert
Guided keeps the analyst in one wizard workspace and presents four fixed prompts at
each step: GOAL, DO NOW, LOOK FOR and NEXT STEP. Deep Analysis provides inline Actor
Compare, relationship, MITRE/TTP, campaign and trend interpretation to avoid opening
unnecessary windows. Expert opens full CAMT workspaces for deeper analysis.

Color coding
Steps have a recognizable color strip. Candidate rows use semantic colors for
Validation, Discovery, Review, Excluded and Unreviewed. This is analyst UX only;
color never changes the similarity score.

Smaller screens
Tool windows are bounded to available desktop space. Bottom wizard navigation remains
a fixed action bar. CAMT automatically reduces an oversized historical minimum window
size on smaller displays without a Windows-only dependency.

Analyst decision
CAMT proposes a fingerprint and analysis profile. The analyst can change both before
the similarity engine runs. Actors already known from the source can be selected as
Control Group and are marked Validation. Other candidates remain Unreviewed until the
analyst selects Unreviewed, Validation, Discovery, Review or Excluded.

Analyst Notes
A free analyst note can be stored for each candidate. Disposition and note remain in
the canonical Supported Behavioral Match result and appear in the generated report.

Interpretation
Discovery means CAMT proposes a candidate for deeper research based on shared behavior.
It is not actor attribution or proof of involvement.
actor_fingerprint:
Behavioral Actor Fingerprint & Similarity

Purpose
An actor is represented as a behavioral fingerprint rather than only a name, IOC set or vendor-specific classification.

Fingerprint dimensions
- ATT&CK;
- ATT&CK ICS;
- sectors;
- malware;
- tools;
- campaigns;
- initial access;
- target assets;
- protocols;
- IT→OT movement;
- negative evidence.

Analyses
Actor → Actor compares a selected actor with other actor profiles.
Observed Behavior → Actors uses observed techniques and investigation context and returns a Top-N behavioral-similarity ranking.

Supported JSON
CAMT accepts a flat fingerprint such as:
  {"techniques":["T1190"],"sectors":["energy"],"target_assets":["hmi"]}
and a structured fingerprint such as:
  {"actor":"Sandworm Team / ELECTRUM",
   "fingerprint":{"techniques":["T1190"],"sectors":["energy"],"target_assets":["hmi"]}}

Supported fields are techniques, ics_techniques, sectors, malware, tools, campaigns,
initial_access, target_assets, protocols, it_ot_movement and negative_evidence;
confidence is optional. If no usable dimension is found, CAMT stops with a clear
validation message instead of producing artificial 0% matches.

Coverage
Similarity is calculated only across dimensions for which both observed context and
the candidate actor contain data. Missing data is 'No data', not 0% overlap. Coverage
shows comparable/reference dimensions.

Negative evidence
Explicit contradictory observations can reduce the similarity score.

Supported Behavioral Match Engine
Default ranking uses Supported Match Score, not Raw Similarity alone.

Raw Similarity measures overlap within comparable fingerprint dimensions.
Coverage measures how many populated observed dimensions can be compared with the
candidate. An actor with 90% Raw Similarity on only 1/8 dimensions can therefore rank
below an actor with 75% similarity and 7/8 coverage.

Evidence Quality uses explicit source/evidence quality from an Intelligence Pack when
available; otherwise actor confidence is used as a conservative fallback.

Supporting Evidence shows concrete overlap in ATT&CK/ICS techniques, sectors, initial
access, target assets, tooling, malware, campaigns, protocols and IT→OT movement.

Missing / Unknown Evidence means the observed dimension is known but Actor Library has
no candidate data. It is not treated as a mismatch.

Contradictory Evidence uses only explicit negative_evidence that actually appears in
the candidate profile. Missing knowledge is not treated as contradiction.

Analytical Confidence (HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW) combines Supported Match, coverage and
evidence quality. It is a quality signal for the comparison, not a probability that
the actor is responsible.

Why this match?
Double-click a candidate to view Matched Evidence, Contradictory Evidence,
Missing/Unknown Evidence, Fingerprint Coverage, Score Breakdown and Sources/Provenance.

Analyst Disposition & Notes
Candidates can be marked Unreviewed, Validation, Discovery, Review or Excluded. A free
Analyst Note can be stored for each candidate. These fields are filterable and remain
with the canonical result.

Canonical Result
Each analysis is stored once as the canonical Supported Behavioral Match result in the
Intelligence Module Framework result store. Trend Watch, Report Studio and an Active
Team Case use this same result object instead of recalculating the ranking independently.

Structured Observed Context example:
  {
    "actor": "Observed OT intrusion",
    "fingerprint": {
      "techniques": ["T1190", "T1078", "T1105"],
      "ics_techniques": ["T0853"],
      "sectors": ["energy"],
      "initial_access": ["exploit-public-facing-application"],
      "target_assets": ["hmi", "engineering-workstation"],
      "tools": [], "malware": [], "campaigns": [], "protocols": [],
      "it_ot_movement": ["enterprise-to-ot"],
      "negative_evidence": [], "confidence": 85
    }
  }

Interpretation
Use terms such as Best Supported Behavioral Match and Potentially Related Tradecraft.
When coverage/evidence is insufficient, CAMT uses Insufficient Evidence for Attribution.
A Supported Match is never automatically actor attribution, identity, sponsorship,
responsibility or proof of involvement.
data_consistency:
CAMT contains multiple workspaces that use the same investigation data. The principle is one canonical source per data category.

Network
The current NetMap / Asset Repository is authoritative for network observations.
Asset Intelligence, Digital Twin and reporting should read the same assets and relationships.

CVE
The local Offline Intelligence SQLite database is authoritative for standalone CVE
correlation. Team CVE Repository Sync creates a controlled central copy and does not overwrite the local database.

Team
Case objects are revisioned on Team Server. Local source data is not silently replaced by a central save.

Reports
Diagrams and tables should come from the same analysis snapshot. If screens differ,
first verify the active case, scan, scenario and mode.

troubleshooting:
Startup
Run CAMT from source with run_camt.bat before rebuilding PyInstaller. Startup exceptions are stored in the CAMT log directory.

Workspace
If Home unexpectedly shows zero capabilities, verify active build_git.py, assets/workspace, module registry readability and core navigation contributions.

Repository
If package listing fails, inspect the callback/crash report first. Artwork loading is optional presentation logic and must never break navigation.

Digital Twin localization
Literal keys such as dt.new_empty indicate a source/locale mismatch.

Help
Help is language-specific. Verify src/projectmanager/help_content/en.json and nl.json in the active source.

Ctrl+Home
Return to CAMT Home / Workspace.

Ctrl+Shift+P
Open Command Palette where supported.

Enter
Activate the focused search/default action in many dialogs.

Esc
Close or cancel supported secondary dialogs.

Mouse wheel

repository:
Repository is the discovery and management entry for CAMT modules and plugins.

Package states
- Installed
- Available
- Update available
- Disabled/blocked where applicable

Presentation
Repository/package metadata can provide category, description, artwork, version, package URL and SHA-256. Missing artwork must never block package installation or navigation.

Offline
Installed modules remain available offline. Repository discovery/download requires connectivity unless packages are imported manually.
licensing:
CAMT supports Evaluation, Basic, Professional and Team licenses.

Edition identity
The visible product name is derived from the active license instead of being permanently hardcoded as Professional Edition.

Entitlements
Licenses determine access to modules, plugins and Team-only functions. Enforcement remains central and is not based on presentation alone.
guided_network_analysis:
Guided Network Analysis

Purpose
This short workflow helps a user perform a basic NetMap discovery and continue through CAMT analysis without introducing a second scanner. It uses the existing NetMap scan, service/version, vulnerability-analysis and Report Studio context functions.

Workflow
1. Discover — open the Scan Wizard and choose Local Interface, VPN/Routed Network or Jump Host/SSH. Confirm authorization and complete Preflight.
2. Review topology — inspect discovered hosts, device classifications, routes and the visual network map.
3. Identify services — when authorized and necessary, run service/version detection on discovered hosts.
4. Correlate findings — run Vulnerability Analysis. Treat CVE results as candidates until exact product/version evidence confirms them.
5. Interpret — use Analysis Advice to review observations, exposure categories, analysis stage, CVE correlation and next actions.
6. Report — prepare the shared network analysis context for Report Studio.

Safety and evidence
Only scan networks and hosts for which you have authorization. A discovered host or open port is an observation, not proof of compromise. Cached or unconfirmed assets should be revalidated. Vulnerability matches remain candidates until supporting product/version evidence is available.

Where to start
From CAMT Home/command palette choose Guided Network Analysis, or in NetMap choose Discover > Guided Network Analysis.
